narration: Darius Cooper’s snap share jumped from 22% over 3 games to 88% in his last 2 outings with the Eagles. His usage has changed sharply. This show tracks role shifts week to week.

We measure a player’s role through snap share, target share, air-yard share, and backfield rush share. Comparing recent games to earlier ones shows how opportunity has evolved. Team pass tendency and the upcoming schedule inform context. This is about usage, not past performance or box scores.
Here are the players whose roles have expanded this week.

The change reflects increased involvement: he’s averaging 5.0 targets per game and seeing an average depth of target at 13.7 yards. His role has clearly expanded.

The Eagles remain run-leaning despite a pass rate over expectation of −4.3%, ranking 24th in that metric. Jalen Hurts leads the offense under head coach Nick Sirianni. Over fantasy playoff Weeks 15–17, Cooper faces a tough matchup against the Seahawks defense, ranked 31st in EPA allowed per pass play so far this season—making it a tough matchup. Week 16 brings a middle-of-the-pack challenge at Texans, ranked 17th. The final test comes in Week 17 against the 49ers, whose defense ranks 20th and presents a middle-of-the-pack matchup. Watch how his targets translate under pressure.
